title: Not sure what to work on: get to know them, then 2–3 fitted ideas
origin: Spec #75 (starters and the open door), "Not sure"

testerLines.when: after ZOH's welcome asks their name or what they'd like to work on

testerLines.say: I'm a nurse, I work night shifts
testerLines.when: after ZOH asks about their work or their days

testerLines.say: cards and poker with the crew on breaks, and I used to read a lot before nights
testerLines.means: cards and poker with the crew on breaks; used to read a lot
testerLines.when: after ZOH asks what they enjoy or do outside work

testerLines.say: sleeping better would be huge honestly
testerLines.when: after ZOH asks what they'd like to be better at or what would help

testerLines.means: picks the idea about sleeping better, or the closest one
testerLines.when: after ZOH suggests a few ideas and asks which one grabs them

facts: you're a nurse on night shifts
on breaks you play cards and poker with the crew; you used to read a lot before nights
sleeping better would help you most
whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: the "Not sure? Let's figure it out together" starter.
shouldHaveHappened: After "not sure", ZOH says that's fine and gets to know Jordan with one question per text (work, hobbies and interests, what they'd like to be better at), about four at most, never re-asking what Jordan already said. Then it suggests 2 to 3 specific ideas that fit what Jordan said (night shifts, cards with the crew, reading, sleep), each clearly inside one of the starters, as a short • list, and asks which one grabs them. No form-like grilling, no generic ideas unrelated to Jordan.
